Performance is fine: 10^6 packets with 2048 rules takes 15.85s (mostly request parsing/JSON overhead). 

Note the benchmark sends one packet per chunk (100k requests) — the JSON parsing dominates. Real workloads would have bigger chunks.

Let me also test with more flows (4096 flows) to check the per-flow memory and the heap performance.

Also let me check the checkpoint size with 4096 flows.

Let me run a test with 4096 flows and a checkpoint.

cat > /app/tmp/work/bench2.py <<'PYEOF'
import json, os, random, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/tmp/work')
from bench import build_config

SUB = "/app/submission/main.py"
PY = sys.executable

config = build_config(50, 4)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    p = subprocess.run([PY, "-I", SUB, "compile"], input=json.dumps(config).encode(),
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "program.json")
    open(path,'wb').write(p.stdout)
    reqs = []
    t = 0
    NF = 4096
    for f in range(NF):
        reqs.append({"op":"open","flow":f,"time":t})
    rng = random.Random(3)
    pkts = []
    for i in range(200000):
        t += 1
        pkts.append({"flow":rng.randrange(NF),"time":t,"source":rng.randint(0,1),"length":rng.randint(1,2048)})
    # feed in chunks of 1000
    for i in range(0, len(pkts), 1000):
        reqs.append({"op":"chunk","packets":pkts[i:i+1000]})
    reqs.append({"op":"checkpoint"})
    data = ("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in reqs)+"\n").encode()
    t0=time.time()
    p2 = subprocess.run([PY,"-I",SUB,"stream",path], input=data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    el = time.time()-t0
    print("rc", p2.returncode, "time %.2f" % el, "stderr", p2.stderr.decode()[-500:])
    lines = p2.stdout.decode().splitlines()
    cp = json.loads(lines[-1])["checkpoint"]
    canon = json.dumps(cp, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True).encode('ascii')
    print("flows:", len(cp["fl"]), "canonical checkpoint bytes:", len(canon),
          "limit:", 512 + 8192*len(cp["fl"]), "ok:", len(canon) <= 512+8192*len(cp["fl"]))
    # nested depth
    def depth(v):
        if isinstance(v, dict): return 1 + max([depth(x) for x in v.values()] or [0])
        if isinstance(v, list): return 1 + max([depth(x) for x in v] or [0])
        return 0
    print("depth:", depth(cp))
    # restore and continue
    reqs2 = [{"op":"restore","checkpoint":cp}]
    t += 1
    reqs2.append({"op":"chunk","packets":[{"flow":rng.randrange(NF),"time":t,"source":0,"length":100}]})
    data2 = ("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in reqs2)+"\n").encode()
    t0=time.time()
    p3 = subprocess.run([PY,"-I",SUB,"stream",path], input=data2, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    print("restore rc", p3.returncode, "time %.2f"%(time.time()-t0), p3.stdout.decode()[:400], p3.stderr.decode()[-300:])
PYEOF
cd /app/tmp/work && timeout 900 python3 bench2.py
